Timing: last year's 1H release was stamped 15:30 on 2025-11-14 (https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/8411_20251114_act_20251114_153045_4), and 15:30 JST on 11-13 is 01:30 ET on 11-13. That is after the 11-12 US close and before the 11-13 US open, so the release falls inside the window. EDGAR shows no 6-K after 2026-09-24, so nothing has been pre-released. One stale aggregator date (RTTNews via ad-hoc-news 2026-10-21: 'November 5') is superseded. Tokyo's 11-13 session closes at 15:30 JST, before the results, so the ADR is the first venue to trade the print.
conviction_note: The company guide of ¥1.4trn net assumes a 1.00% BOJ rate, and the BOJ moved to 1.25% on 2026-09-18. Mizuho has raised its guide at each of its last three prints and its CET1 has room, so a guide raise and a new buyback are the likely outcome. The market expects both: the ordinary-profit consensus implies about ¥1.46trn net, and the stock ran up 8.4% in five days into the print. So p_up is only 55 on a 3.5% abs move (+0.35), while the findings' own sizes sum to +0.9. The gap exists because the raise is the expected outcome, not a surprise.

At Q1's net/ordinary ratio of 0.706 that implies roughly ¥1.46trn net, about 4% above the guide. That conversion is my inference, not a published net consensus. findings.finding: Mizuho's own FY2026 outlook (¥1,400bn net, ¥1,750bn net business profit) is stated on its IR Day slide as 'Assuming BOJ Policy Rate of 1.00%'. The BOJ raised to 1.25% on 2026-09-18, effective 09-24, and said it will keep hiking. So the 1H release (the first print since) carries a mechanical case to raise the guide again. Q1 net of ¥422.9bn was already 30% of the raised guide. Mizuho raised its guide at the last three prints: ¥1.02→1.13trn at 1H FY25, above a ¥1.07trn consensus, and ¥1.3→1.4trn at Q1 FY26. The market expects a raise: the inferred net consensus is about ¥1.46trn, roughly 4% above the guide. A raise to about ¥1.45-1.50trn is at consensus; one above ¥1.5trn would beat it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 guide raise of ¥100bn plus a doubled buyback (released 2026-07-30 at 15:30 JST): Tokyo 8411 rose up to +6.29% intraday the next session (https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOFL311L00R30C26A7000000/, 2026-07-31). The 1H FY25 raise to ¥1.13trn beat the ¥1.07trn estimate (https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/mizuho-financial-TYO:8411/news/japan-apos-s-mizuho-books-44-rise-in-second-quarter-profit-raises-forecast-019e69f6-422f-7bfa-b2e1-d9c72139c6c6/); I found no ADR reaction for that day. The baseline carries no earnings-day history (sweep: untrustworthy).
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (Mizuho IR Day 2026 deck; footnote 'Assuming BOJ Policy Rate of 1.00%')
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The BOJ hike is public, and the ordinary-profit consensus already sits above the company guide. The stock rose 8.4% in five days into the print. What is not priced is the size of the raise. If the market had fully priced a large raise, the stock would sit near its 52-week high rather than 11% below it and under its 50-day MA. Even with the raise at consensus, the 1.00% → 1.25% assumption gap is a company-document reason for the raise to clear it.
findings.independence: BOJ decision to 1.25% on 2026-09-18 (https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/9/18/japans-interest-rate-hiked-to-31-year-high-at-1-25-as-inflation-rises). The street ordinary-profit consensus above the implied guide (https://kabuyoho.jp/report?bcode=8411) is a different source pointing the same way. The guide-raise history is part of the same reasoning, merged here rather than filed twice.

findings.finding: The ¥200bn buyback (doubled on 2026-07-30, 35M shares, 1.4% of shares outstanding) ran only to 2026-09-30, so Mizuho has no live authorization going into the print. Its own IR Day deck shows CET1 at 10.4% at Q1, above the midpoint of its stated operational range ('mid 9-10% to mid 10-11%'), with a 'Total Payout Ratio of 50% or more; stable dividends, flexible buybacks' policy. At ¥1.4trn+ net, 50% payout is ≥¥700bn a year. A new buyback and/or a dividend raise at 1H is likely, and larger if the guide is raised.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback doubling came with the Q1 guide raise and the +6.29% Tokyo intraday move on 2026-07-31; the two cannot be separated. In Nov 2025 a sell-side analyst expected ¥200bn at 1H FY25, so a new buyback was the expected outcome then too.
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (IR Day 2026, slide 6: CET1 10.4% at Q1, operational range, payout policy)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: a 1H buyback is a standard expectation for Japanese megabanks. The unpriced part is size. CET1 above the range midpoint plus a rate tailwind leaves room above the ¥200bn run rate. The stock 11% off its high and below its 50-day MA argues the market is not paying for an outsized return.
findings.independence: Expiry and size of the program: https://simplywall.st/stocks/jp/banks/tse-8411/mizuho-financial-group-shares/news/share-buyback-earnings-beat-and-dividend-hike-could-be-a-gam (July 2026) and https://pulse2.com/mizuho-raises-profit-outlook-%c2%a5100-billion-after-boj-rate-hike-and-doubles-buybacks-to-%c2%a5200-billion/ (2026-08-02). The CET1 and payout facts share the IR Day document with finding 1.

findings.finding: Peers that reported 1H after Mizuho last spoke are running ahead on rate-driven profits. Shizuoka FG raised its FY net forecast to ¥120bn (+33% YoY) on 2026-11-10, its second upward revision this year, citing rising domestic rates, and added a ¥10bn buyback and a dividend raise. Mizuho Leasing, a Mizuho equity-method affiliate, reported 1H net +46.8% and raised its full-year forecast (2026-11-09).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of Mizuho reacting to regional-bank read-throughs. Tokyo 8411 rose +4.5% on 11-10 and +3.1% on 11-11, after Shizuoka's release, so some of this is already in the run-up.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The sector rallied on 11-10/11 after these releases. It is filed because it is a direct counterparty-style confirmation that the September hike is flowing into upward revisions. It would be fully priced if MFG had already regained its 50-day MA and 52-week high.
findings.independence: Mizuho Leasing 1H: https://www.zaikei.co.jp/article/20261109/876695.html (2026-11-09), a different issuer and source. Proxy only: neither is Mizuho's own number.

findings.finding: Global CIB is about 34% of Mizuho's gross profit (IR Day slide 4), and the Jul-Sep quarter was mixed for wholesale/markets. LSEG data showed global IB fees down 19% QoQ, and JPMorgan said IB activity 'moderated somewhat' and missed on lower fixed-income trading. That is a risk to the quality of Mizuho's Q2 beat in its non-NII lines. Net of the rest of the company: domestic NII (rates) and WM fees, the other ~66%, are the lines the guide raise rests on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured for Mizuho on markets/IB softness.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and probably known to bank analysts. Filed because the interim ordinary-profit consensus already implies Q2 (~¥531bn) below Q1 (¥599bn), so the street has some slowdown in. A weaker markets line would show up as a miss on the quarter while the guide is still raised, which is the beat-quality risk.
findings.independence: Proxy (US peers' quarter, LSEG industry data via a summary). Goldman's strong IB print (same Fortune piece) points the other way. GCIB share of gross profit: https://library.mizuhogroup.com/asset/2f9d9ed2-70eb-43b4-b9c4-3171415330bc/fg-investors-financial-briefing_20260907_1.pdf

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: the ADR rose +8.41% over five sessions (baseline), and Tokyo 8411 went from ¥7,547 (11-04) to ¥8,158 (11-12) after a sharp drop on 11-06. The 11-06 drop was blamed on AI-investment-slowdown fears and falling long-term rates. So the guide-raise expectation was bid up in the three sessions before the release, and the bar for a 'beat' on the raise rose with it. MUFG and SMFG report the same day, so the sector print, not Mizuho alone, will move the ADR.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured. In Nov 2025 BofA's bank analyst noted that sector fundamentals were 'well understood' and banks needed 'some new factor' to outperform (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/japan-s-megabanks-seen-posting-solid-q2-profits-on-track-for-record-annual-earnings-ce7d5fd9d989f021, 2025-11-11).
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. It is filed because a short-term run-up into an expected raise is what turns a confirmed raise into a sell-the-news. Short interest is small (2.8 days at 2026-08-14), so there is no squeeze to offset.
findings.independence: Tokyo price path: https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/mizuho-financial-group-8411-t-rises-2026-11-11/ (2026-11-11, +3.14% to ¥8,155), plus the baseline's run_up_5d_pct.

baseline_tension: No option anchor and no skew. The 8.4% five-day run-up agrees with my positive lean, which suggests part of the guide-raise case is already in the price. That is why p_up sits at 55, not in the 60s, even though the rate-assumption gap is a company-document fact.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar unsourced): the net-income consensus is my inference from one ordinary-profit consensus, so the guidance finding is capped from +1.0 to +0.8 and p_up goes from 56 to 55.

Rule 5/9 (proxy; segment net of the rest): the IB/markets softness finding goes from -0.4 to -0.3, because it rests on US peers and GCIB is about a third of gross profit while the NII/WM lines carry the guide.
Rule 1 (fact is not reaction) and rule 7 (positioning): already reflected in the draft through the positioning finding and p_up near 50; no further change, so the lesson is not applied twice.
